articles.summary: New York City FC will relocate its minor league club, bringing MLS NEXT Pro soccer and youth development programs to Middlesex County,
articles.body:
Professional soccer is coming to Middlesex County.

New York City FC II — the minor league affiliate for New York City FC's Major League Soccer franchise — will relocate to a new 6,500-seat stadium in Edison, with play beginning in July 2027. The new MLS NEXT Pro team will eventually take on its own name, colors and identity.

The club, which will initially be called New Jersey MLS NEXT Pro, will play at the NEXUS sports and entertainment district on the grounds next to Middlesex College.

New York City FC II, commonly known as NYCFC II , is the reserve team of New York City FC and competes in MLS NEXT Pro, a professional men's soccer league in the United States and Canada affiliated with the MLS. The league, classified as part of the third tier of the U.S. soccer system, was launched in 2022 to complete the professional player pathway from youth academies to MLS teams.

The league is in its fifth season and has 30 teams — 27 affiliated with MLS clubs and three independent teams. More MLS-affiliated and independent clubs are expected to join in the coming years, including teams in Long Island, Cleveland, Jacksonville, Florida and Grand Rapids, Mich.

As the New York City FC minor league affiliate, NYCFC II provides a pathway for developing players to gain professional experience before potentially advancing to New York City FC's MLS roster. NYCFC II currently plays at Belson Stadium on the campus of St. John's University in Queens, while also hosting a series of matches at Icahn Stadium on Randall's Island.

The arrival of professional soccer is part of a broader push by Middlesex County to establish itself as a destination for sports, entertainment and education, officials said.

NEXUS, a $350 million sports and entertainment district that includes a stadium scheduled for a ribbon-cutting later this year, is one piece of a larger county investment that also includes the development of a multipurpose community venue and student center on the Middlesex College campus.

"New Jersey is a soccer state, and we're proud to welcome our newest professional soccer club to Middlesex County and NEXUS,'' New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill said in a statement. "Starting next summer, New Jerseyans will get to see elite soccer played in our own backyard. Bringing professional soccer to NEXUS gives fans in the heart of our state a team to rally behind while creating new opportunities for athletes and strengthening our state's growing sports economy.''

Not everyone is celebrating, however. State Sen. Declan O'Scanlon, R-Monmouth, questioned the use of public money to help finance the sports complex.

O'Scanlon said $200 million in state taxpayer dollars and COVID relief funds went toward the project, arguing that the money could have been better directed toward struggling families and businesses and the state's affordability challenges.

"$200 million of taxpayer dollars went into the sports complex home for the soccer team's wealthy owners, including COVID relief money, and this is what we're celebrating, a minor-league soccer team? Families and business suffered during COVID and are struggling with soaring electric bills, property taxes, and daily costs of living,'' O'Scanlon, the Republican state Senate budget officer, said. "Claiming this is a success and hiding the $200 million waste of taxpayer and COVID relief money behind the ribbon cutting is a slap in the face to people who want our state to focus on affordability. Minor-league mentality gets you minor-league results. New Jersey taxpayers deserve better."

The multipurpose venue, being developed as a home field for the Rutgers University baseball team , is scheduled to welcome the Scarlet Knights beginning next year. Plans include broadcast-streaming capabilities suitable for the Big Ten Network.

The New Jersey MLS NEXT Pro club will be the first MLS NEXT Pro team launched under the Hometown Soccer Holdings platform. MLS and investment firm KKR announced a strategic investment in the league in April, creating Hometown Soccer Holdings as a commercial engine intended to help develop new stadiums, establish club brands and improve the fan experience.

The Middlesex County club is the first expansion announcement under that initiative.

"Professional soccer belongs in communities like Middlesex County, New Jersey," said Tom Glick, CEO of Hometown Soccer Holdings. "The county's remarkable diversity, deep soccer culture, and passion for the game make this the right place to build something lasting. We are proud to make New Jersey MLS NEXT Pro our first club under the Hometown Soccer platform and to partner with New York City FC to deliver a world-class experience for fans and families across New Jersey."

For Middlesex County , the new soccer stadium will add another piece to that emerging sports landscape. In addition to the stadium, the complex includes recreational fields, an adjacent plaza and a restaurant and bar. The stadium will feature suites, two upper-level party decks, a premium bar overlooking the field and a large grass hill with a playground designed to give families another place to watch games.

The facility sits within walking distance of NEXUS Fields at Thomas A. Edison Park, a 14-field youth soccer complex expected to become a major tournament destination.

Beginning next year, New York City FC plans to establish a youth soccer club in Middlesex County serving children ages 3 through 18. The youth program will give local players access to New York City FC's coaching methodology and player-development system, according to Brad Sims, CEO of New York City FC.

"New York City FC has always been committed to developing the next generation of local soccer players and fans," Sims said. "We look forward to creating new opportunities for local players to enter the New York City FC development pathway, and building on our legacy of developing top talent."

The pro franchise will connect local youth players to one of MLS's established development systems, according to Middlesex County Commissioner Director Ronald Rios.

"Bringing professional soccer to Middlesex County, and its almost 900,000 residents, will make us an exciting new sports destination in New Jersey," he said.

At the 2025 stadium groundbreaking, Rios called the project a milestone in the county's Community, Innovation and Opportunity plan, while then-Gov. Phil Murphy said the facility would serve as a hub for learning, recreation, entertainment and community events.

The stadium's location also is expected to make the soccer club accessible beyond Middlesex County. NEXUS is on Route 514 in Edison, approximately two miles from the New Jersey Turnpike, Garden State Parkway and Route 287.

New Jersey soccer fans still reeling from this summer's World Cup games at MetLife Stadium can also expect youth tournaments, college and high school games, and community events involving MLS and MLS NEXT Pro players, officials said.

"Fans from across the country will come for the soccer and stay for all the food, shopping, and entertainment that the Heart of New Jersey has to offer,'' Sherrill said. "We're proud to welcome this club to Middlesex County and can't wait to see fans in the stands at NEXUS."

articles.title: Injured Barcelona midfielder will resume training tomorrow as he prepares to return vs Valencia
articles.summary: As FC Barcelona get set to kickstart their preparations for their next La Liga game, they have been greeted with some positive news on the injury front. Inde...
articles.body:
As FC Barcelona get set to kickstart their preparations for their next La Liga game, they have been greeted with some positive news on the injury front.

Indeed, according to SPORT , Barcelona midfielder Gavi is set to return to the pitch on Thursday and is expected to complete a significant part of the training session alongside his teammates.

It represents an important step forward after the scare he suffered in the opening game of the La Liga season against Elche.

Gavi took a heavy blow to his right leg during the match and subsequently began experiencing discomfort. Barcelona's medical staff decided to withdraw him before half-time as a precaution.

The concern was understandable given that it was the same leg in which he previously suffered an ACL injury.

However, subsequent tests ruled out any significant damage and confirmed that the La Masia graduate had suffered nothing more than a contusion.

One step closer to returning. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images)

Since then, Gavi has missed Barcelona's two league games against Athletic Club and Rayo Vallecano.

The midfielder has followed an individual programme aimed at fully resolving the discomfort. That moment is now getting closer .

Gavi is now expected to take part in Thursday's training session with his teammates, although Barcelona have no intention of rushing his recovery.

The priority is for him to gradually regain his confidence and match fitness.

Nonetheless, a place on the squad list for next weekend's trip to face Valencia cannot yet be ruled out, but his progress over the coming days will determine whether he is ready to return to competitive action.

An important player for Barcelona. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images)

Gavi's recovery is important for Barcelona, considering that Flick considers him one of the key players in his squad.

A fiery competitor, Gavi's importance for the Blaugrana goes beyond what he contributes during matches.

Indeed, while the coaching staff greatly value his technical ability, intensity and competitive mentality, they place even greater emphasis on his character and influence within the dressing room.

That is why his return to the training pitch represents such welcome news for Barcelona. His progress during the next few training sessions will ultimately determine when he can return to full availability for Flick.

articles.title: "Todo está trazado para que el Mallorca no sufra económicamente si no ascendemos"
articles.standfirst: Alfonso Díaz, CEO del club, y Pablo Ortells, director deportivo, analizaron el mercado que han realizado, dejando claro que "hay plantilla de sobra para competir"
articles.summary: Alfonso Díaz, CEO del club, y Pablo Ortells, director deportivo, analizaron el mercado que han realizado, dejando claro que "hay plantilla de sobra para competir"
articles.body: El Mallorca ha cerrado un mercado histórico. Más de 60 millones de euros ingresados en ventas tras descender. Es el conjunto que más ha recaudado en este siglo después de perder la categoría. Pablo Ortells ha respondido firmando a 13 futbolistas con el único objetivo de ascender. Muchos de los nuevos fichajes han llegado cedidos con opción de compra, por lo que puede sorprender que los baleares no hayan invertido más. En este sentido, Alfonso Díaz, CEO del club, aclaró que han "utilizado todo lo que tenían de límite salarial" y detalló la hoja de ruta para rearmar el proyecto y potenciar la plantilla lo máximo posible: "Siempre queda algo para invierno, pero el límite salarial está prácticamente todo invertido. De los más de 60 millones que se comentan por ventas, no siempre llega la cantidad neta al club y tenemos que cubrir unos 50 millones de diferencia de ingresos con la Primera. Tenemos una ayuda por descenso. Luego inviertes en jugadores. Hay que tener en cuenta que la pérdida de ingresos por bajar se pierde en una temporada y las ventas de jugadores las vas cobrando en dos o tres. Además, todos los jugadores que hemos firmado con opción de compra se tienen que poder pagar el año que viene. No todo es tan bonito como puede parecer". Pero no sólo se han firmado todos los jugadores posibles para gozar de una plantilla amplia, sino que se ha realizado un esfuerzo por mantener a futbolistas como Pablo Torre o Sergi Darder: "Es muy importante que se queden jugadores con nivel de Primera división, pero más allá de acuerdos económicos o contractuales, lo que ha pesado es su compromiso con el club y el proyecto", explicó Ortells. Para el director deportivo bermellón, "hay equipo de sobra para competir", aunque no se mojó sobre si es la mejor plantilla de la categoría, de la misma manera que Díaz evitó contestar si sería un fracaso no ascender teniendo en cuenta el poder económico: "Eso ya se verá a final de temporada". Una de las máximas preocupaciones de los aficionados es cómo podría afectar a las arcas del club el hecho de no ascender al primer año: "Lo importante es que en estos cinco años en Primera se han hecho las inversiones adecuadas para tener un equipo fuerte que desgraciadamente descendió. El club tenía un patrimonio y hemos podido rearmar el proyecto. Si permanecemos en Segunda, ya hablaremos, pero todo está trazado para no sufrir económicamente en caso de no ascender", aseguró Díaz. Ortells fue el gran señalado de la temporada pasada tras el descenso. La plantilla se quedó muy corta y Demichelis tuvo que tirar de canteranos en partidos clave por la permanencia. El director deportivo asumió este verano que necesitaba formar una plantilla larga, con 29 fichas de primer equipo: "Hay parones de selecciones en los que puedes perder jugadores, sanciones, lesiones… Lo importante es que el míster tenga para elegir en un contexto de competencia sana que haga progresar a los futbolistas, y que luchen por ser titulares. Entre esas 29 fichas, tenemos muchos chicos del filial que vienen haciéndolo bien. Tendrán sus oportunidades y ojalá puedan ayudar al equipo".

articles.title: Why Folarin Balogun's Everton move collapsed on Deadline Day leaving Toffees, Chelsea and Monaco frustrated
articles.summary: Sky Sports News takes you inside why Folarin Balogun's move to Everton collapsed on Deadline Day to leave the Toffees, Chelsea and Monaco upset; before Balogun's decision, Monaco had pulled the plug on a deal for midfielder Lamine Camara to join Chelsea as their Enzo Fernandez replacement
articles.body:
Chelsea , Everton and Monaco ended up very frustrated as Folarin Balogun opted against joining Everton at the last minute after Monaco had earlier pulled out of a deal to sell Lamine Camara to Chelsea, who wanted the midfielder as their Enzo Fernandez replacement.

The two Premier League sides were particularly left fuming about the situation.

Here, Sky Sports News takes you inside why both deals collapsed on a dramatic end to Deadline Day…

Monaco needed to make a sale to help resolve a debt issue, while Everton needed a striker.

Balogun became a solution for both parties, and a £40m agreement was reached - but then came the first issue with the deal.

There was a problem with the USA international's medical after Everton found evidence of an injury, which Monaco and the player refuted, claiming he was fit to play immediately.

With the 11pm deadline approaching, Everton decided to proceed with the transfer but attempted to renegotiate the deal on cheaper terms in case the injury left him unable to play.

The club-to-club deal became much more performance-related, with clauses inserted that meant Monaco would get less money if Balogun could not play.

Crucially, it is understood nothing changed with Balogun's personal terms.

How Everton's Zirkzee move angers Balogun

Amid a renegotiation of the Balogun deal, Chelsea reached an agreement with Monaco to sign midfielder Camara as a replacement for Fernandez, who was set to join Manchester City in a joint-British record £125m deal.

Meanwhile, Everton made a loan offer for Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee , which was rejected.

Sky Sports News understands Everton offered to pay a total fee of around £10m for Zirkzee, which included his wages for the season and a loan fee.

But the feeling at Old Trafford was that Everton's approach came too late and was not of value.

The Toffees' pursuit of Zirkzee is what upset Balogun, who felt the club were going behind his back to sign someone else.

Balogun's unhappiness with Everton was revealed by Monaco chief Thiago Scuro at a press conference on Wednesday.

He said: "Balogun's allegation is that I'm not feeling well because of the way the club treated me.

"I'm not feeling well because Everton's medical department brought doubts about my future or my health.

"I have nothing (no medical problem), so I'm not comfortable to sign a long contract here."

Everton are understood to be surprised at the allegation that Balogun was made to feel unwanted, given they never renegotiated his personal terms and clearly wanted to get the deal done.

The renegotiation of the guaranteed fee payable to Monaco justified the risk given the issue with the medical.

Sky Sports News also understands that Everton's interest in Zirkzee was separate from the Balogun deal, with the club prepared to sign both players.

Everton feel the ex-Arsenal forward misunderstood their Zirkzee approach - they were not turning their attention to a different player.

Believing Balogun would be joining Everton, Monaco pulled the plug on Chelsea's deal for Camara.

The Ligue 1 side preferred selling Balogun over Camara because they only needed the money from one player sale.

But Balogun then sensationally decided to walk away from his Everton move over what he perceived as poor treatment from the Merseysiders.

His dramatic decision, which saw him miss out on his dream Premier League move, meant all three clubs were left disappointed.

Monaco kept both Balogun and Camara, failing to raise the money they wanted.

Everton missed out on signing a striker, leaving them with just one recognised striker, Thierno Barry , in their squad after selling Beto to Fiorentina in a £15.4m Deadline Day deal.

And Chelsea were left with no Fernandez replacement after he joined Man City - a deal which the Blues could have pulled out of but honoured despite having no replacement.

The question now is whether these deals could be revived in January? Well, you would say it is unlikely after this shambles.
